To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mitochondria‐ rich cell membrane contains a population of Cl‐ channels of high unitary conductance that are activated by cell depolarizations and clamping of the cell potential to positive values.
mitochondria‐rich (MRC) cells of toad bladder have a large number of Cl‐ channels with large single channel conductance and that the channel conductance increases as a function of membrane voltage.

mitochondria‐rich (epithelial) cells have large unitary chloride channels with conductances of 200‐300 pico‐Siemens and that the chloride channels of the mitochondria‐‐rich cell membrane are activated in excess of a Goldman‐Hodkin‐Katz‐type rectification by depolarization of the cell membrane potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chloride currents of mitochondria‐rich (M‐rich) cells of toad epithelium.
the properties of Cl‐ channels in mitochondria‐rich (M‐R) cells of amphibian skin epithelium, and the possible role of these channels in epithelial chloride secretion.

the mitochondria‐ rich cells of toad urinary bladder epithelium possess a large number of Cl‐ channels with a single channel conductance of at least 200 pS and a mean open time of about 0.5 ms.
mitochondria‐rich skin epithelial cells contain Cl‐ channels of very large unitary conductances.
the mitochondria‐‐rich cells of the toad skin epithelial membrane contain a population of large unitary Cl‐ channels which are activated by cell depolarizing membrane potentials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitochondria‐ric cell membrane is permeable to Cl‐ and that the permeability is controlled by membrane potential.
mitochondria‐rich skin cells contain a large population of chloride channels with a conductance of about 300 pS.
the mitochondria‐ rich cells of toad bladder have a high Cl‐ conductance with large single channel conductance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondria‐rich (MRC) cells of toad urinary bladder have a large conductance Cl‐ channel with an open probability of about 0.5 at the resting membrane potential.
the mitochondria‐dense cell of toad skin is a good model for studying the properties and regulation of Cl‐ channels of the apical membrane of epithelia.
